references.text: Joseph interprets the cupbearer's dream and predicts that he will be restored to his position within three days – which is fulfilled at Pharaoh's birthday feast.
Joseph also interprets the baker's dream and predicts his execution within three days – which is fulfilled at Pharaoh's birthday feast.
The king sent word and released Joseph – parallel to how Pharaoh 'lifted up the head' of his servants and decided their fate on his birthday.
Herod celebrates his birthday with a feast for his nobles, and John the Baptist's head is presented – a strong parallel to Pharaoh's birthday feast where the baker's fate was sealed.
The direct fulfillment of Joseph's interpretations: the cupbearer was restored and the baker was hanged, just as Joseph had predicted.
Clear parallel: A royal birthday feast serving as the climax for the execution of an innocent servant.
